validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed clean. This row is one of five WBI Energy Transmission FERC-certificated segments (Docket CP20-52) that together make up the North Bakken Expansion Project: Tioga-Elkhorn Creek (P3584, 62.8 mi/24in), Line Section 25 Loop (P3585, 20.3 mi/12in), Line Section 30 Loop (P3586, this row, 9.6 mi/12in), Tioga Compressor Lateral (P3587, 0.5 mi/20in), Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border interconnect (P3588, 0.3 mi/24in). Sum = 93.5 mi, which matches the FERC Federal Register Notice of Application (2020-04321) verbatim: 'about 93.5 miles of new 24-, 20-, and 12-inch-diameter pipeline, pipeline looping, and 0.1 mile of pipeline replacement' -- this is independent, primary confirmation the 5-way segment split is correct and none of the rows duplicate another (cross-checked against the full 46-row roster: no other row plausibly matches this geography). Not a duplicate of anything else in the roster (Williston Basin/Bakken cluster is otherwise Bison, Williston Basin mainline, Northern Border, Valley Expansion, Traill County, Doosan Bobcat, South Saskatchewan Access -- all distinct systems/interconnects, not this project). Classification (gas transmission loop) confirmed by the FERC EA facility description and by NS Energy Business. Location confirmed: Williams County, North Dakota, from the existing Nesson Valve Setting to the Tioga Compressor Station (FERC EA pp.10-11; NS Energy Business). Existence is not in doubt -- this is one of the best-documented rows in the batch (FERC docket, two independent news outlets on completion, an operator project page, and a trade database all agree). Opened/read to exhaustion: FERC CP20-52 Draft EA (29MB, searched full text for all 5 segment names, MAOP, dates, cost), NS Energy Business project page, WBI Energy's own North Bakken project page, the archived Williston Herald article, KFYR-TV and Prairie Public Broadcasting completion stories, the MDU Resources investor press release, and the FERC Federal Register Notice of Application. 8 of the row's 8 harvested wiki citations were opened (the Willistonherald.com live URL is dead/404 -- superseded here by its Wayback capture; the eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php citation is a generic EIA data-portal root, not an article about this pipeline, and was not usable as a ref).

validity.recommendation: Capacity=250 MMcf/d on this row is the PROJECT-wide incremental design capacity restated on the segment row, not a value specific to the 9.6-mile Line Section 30 Loop -- flag rather than fix (no segment-specific throughput figure exists for a looping segment). Same figure is restated identically on siblings P3584/P3585/P3587/P3588 -- see cross_row_leads.
validity.researcher_notes: The FERC EA (p.2, Purpose and Need), the Federal Register Notice of Application, WBI Energy's own project page, and NS Energy Business all state '250,000 MMcf/d' / '250 MMcf/d' (the FERC document's own units label is inconsistent -- '250,000 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)' is internally contradictory since MMcf/d already means millions; every other source states plainly 250 MMcf/d) as the INCREMENTAL FIRM TRANSPORTATION DESIGN CAPACITY of the whole North Bakken Expansion Project -- never as a number specific to the Line Section 30 Loop. A loop pipeline built to parallel and de-bottleneck an existing line does not carry an independently measurable capacity of its own; the 250 MMcf/d is what the combined system (Tioga-Elkhorn Creek + both loops + the lateral + the interconnect) was built to add. This is the aggregate-on-a-segment defect flagged in the sweep brief. I did not find, and would not expect to find, a source stating a Line-Section-30-Loop-specific capacity distinct from the project total.

cross_row_leads.facts: Tioga-Elkhorn Creek Pipeline: 62.8 mi (101 km), 24-inch diameter, MAOP 1,480 psig, bi-directional; same FERC docket CP20-52, same Feb 14 2020 filing / Jul 2021 construction / Feb 1 2022 in-service; same 250 MMcf/d project-total capacity issue applies (aggregate-on-segment).

Line Section 25 Loop: 20.3 mi (32.67 km), 12-inch diameter, MAOP 1,098 psig, from Tioga Compressor Station to the new Norse Transfer Station in Burke County; also involves an 8-inch, 700 psig EXISTING Line Section 25 uprate over ~28.3 mi (this is the actual source of NS Energy's '700psig' mention, not this row's Line Section 30 Loop -- don't cross-cite); same 250 MMcf/d project-total capacity issue applies.

Tioga Compressor Lateral: 0.5 mi (800 m), 20-inch diameter, MAOP 1,480 psig, between the new Tioga Plant Receipt Station and new facilities at the Tioga Compressor Station; same 250 MMcf/d project-total capacity issue applies.

Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border interconnect: 0.3 mi (480 m), 24-inch diameter, MAOP 1,480 psig, no new block valves or pig launchers/receivers (only segment in the project without them); same 250 MMcf/d project-total capacity issue applies.
